column1: # boru Language Specification: FN-LOCAL DEFS and SCOPE — what a `def`
# inside a fn body means, and who can see it.
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Family: fn-locals-scope. Written to widen the corpus past the
# one-liner shapes it had. Real .boru files do not call a word with two
# literals; they open a fn body, bind three or four locals, define a
# helper fn beside them, branch, loop, and hand a closure to a callback
# — all in the same body. Every row here is one of those shapes.
# What the family covers: a body defining a local fn and calling it;
# local helpers that recurse (self, mutual, accumulator); a local whose
# value is COMPUTED (from a param, from a previous local, from an `if` /
# `case` / `do` / `codequote`); REDEFINITION inside a body (and `undef`);
# a local SHADOWING a param, a module-level name, an imported module's
# exported word, and an imported module's NAMESPACE; CONDITIONAL defs
# inside a branch; DYNAMIC-SCOPE reads (a callee seeing the caller's
# body-locals and params); a local read by a NESTED body (capture, its
# snapshot rule, and its transitivity); locals driven by `for` / `while`
# / `for-each`; locals that HOLD functions; and frame teardown.
# EVERY row's expected column is the engine's own answer, measured with
# `boru do <input> end canon` on the INTERPRETER (BORU_NO_COMPILE=1) —
# the same canon rendering the spec runner compares against. Nothing
# here is a guess; candidates the interpreter would not run cleanly were
# discarded rather than repaired into something that passes.
# ROWS THAT FAIL TO COMPILE TO COMPILE ARE RECORDED DELIBERATELY, AS OPEN
# DEFECTS. Each such row's description begins `DOES NOT COMPILE:` and ends with
# the exact reason `BORU_FORCE_COMPILE=1 boru do …` printed. They are
# not mistakes and must not be deleted to keep a ceiling green: a
# compile compile failure is WHOLE-PROGRAM and latches on the FIRST unsupported
# construct, which is precisely why the compiler scores ~96% on a corpus
# of 40-character one-liners and ~65% on real files whose median size is
# 10,472 characters. The compile failure texts below are the ledger of what is
# left to build.
# THE LEDGER. 100 rows: 80 compile, 20 decline, 0 diverge. Six of the
# twenty compile failures are ERROR:-column rows (§5, §12) where the check pass
# is simply agreeing with the interpreter that the program is bad —
# those are NOT gaps. The other FOURTEEN are rows with a real value
# that the compiler will not build, grouped by the exact reason it
# printed:
#   6 ×  fn f: body result of unknown provenance
#          — §6: a `def` inside an `if` branch whose name is read after
#            the branch closes. One-sided or two-sided, pre-bound or not,
#            nested or flat: every spelling declines. This is the single
#            biggest gap this family found, and it is the commonest
#            statement in real boru.
#   2 ×  operand of unknown provenance or not statically materialisable at <word>
#          — §6: the same conditionally-def'd local, but consumed by an
#            operator (`add`, `mul`) instead of returned. Different
#            message, same root.
#   2 ×  function value reaches push (Stage 3)
#          — §10: a body-local fn value pushed into a local list, whether
#            written straight or accumulated in a loop. Parking the same
#            value in a local MAP compiles (the row above it), so this is
#            `push` specifically, not fn-values-in-containers.
#   2 ×  check diagnostics: [fn_body_error] … conflicts with an existing type name
#          — §11: a `class` or an `fnsig` declared as a body-local. The
#            interpreter scopes the type to the frame; the check pass sees
#            it as a second global type of that name.
#   1 ×  check diagnostics: [undefined_word] undefined word: n
#          — §9: an `each` callback that redefines a local of the
#            ENCLOSING body. The check pass cannot see the enclosing
#            body-local through the callback boundary at all.
#   1 ×  if: then-branch result of unknown provenance
#          — §6: a body-local fn that RETURNS a closure out of a branch.
# NOTE FOR THE RATCHET: test/go/langspec/compiled_coverage_test.go holds
# a failureCeiling. The declining rows below are NEW EVIDENCE, not
# regressions — the ceiling must be re-based against them.
# TWO COMPILED/INTERPRETED DIVERGENCES were found while writing this
# family. They are NOT rows: a diverging row would break the
# compile==interpret differential gate rather than document a gap, so
# they are recorded here (the convention edge-fns-1.tsv uses) and belong
# in a findings doc, not the corpus.
# (omitted) DIVERGENCE — a local redefined inside a `while` body, read
#   after the loop, is ONE ITERATION AHEAD under the compiler:
#     def f fn [[] [Integer] [def i 0 end while [i lt 3] [def last i end def i (i add 1)] end last]]  f
#   interpreter 2 (correct: the last i the body saw), compiled 3. The
#   top-level spelling without the fn wrapper diverges identically, so
#   the fn frame is not what breaks:
#     def i 0 end while [i lt 3] [def last i end def i (i add 1)] end last
#   interpreter 2, compiled 3.
# (omitted) DIVERGENCE — the loop-carried dynamic read of recursion.tsv
#   §10, with the recursive helper as a BODY-LOCAL and the carried name
#   a body-local of the enclosing frame:
#     def f fn [[] [Integer] [def depth2 0 end def go fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [if (k lte 0) [depth2] [def depth2 (depth2 add 1) end go (k sub 1)]]] go 3]]  f
#   interpreter 3 (each frame's redefinition is visible to the next),
#   compiled 0 (the compiled frames read the enclosing snapshot).
# (omitted) FINDING, not a divergence — `def` of a FN inside a body whose
#   name collides with a module-level fn of the same signature does NOT
#   restore the outer definition at frame exit, where a same-named PARAM
#   does (recursion.tsv §12 pins the param side). Measured, both modes
#   agreeing, so it is not a compiler gap:
#     def add2 fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x add 2]] def f fn [[] [Integer] [def add2 fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x add 100]] add2 1]] f end add2 1
#   answers `101 101` — the second `add2 1` still reaches the body-local.
#   Kept out of the corpus: this is the `def` overlap-redefinition filter
#   of lang/go/CLAUDE.md meeting frame teardown, and pinning it would
#   freeze whichever side turns out to be wrong.
# §1  a fn body DEFINING a local fn and CALLING it
def f fn [[] [Integer] [def helper fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 2]] helper 21]]  f
column3: a body-local fn, defined and called in the same body

column1: def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def helper fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [k mul 2]] def r (helper x) end def s (helper r) end s]]  f 3
column3: the local helper is called twice, each result bound to a further local

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [List] [def helper fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [k mul 2]] each helper/v (iota n)]]  f 4
column3: the body-local fn travels to `each` as a /v value

column1: def f fn [[xs:List] [List] [def bump fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n add 1]] each bump/v xs]]  f [1 2 3]
column3: …over the param list rather than a computed one

column1: def f fn [[xs:List] [Integer] [def sum2 fn [[a:Integer b:Integer] [Integer] [a add b]] def n (0 fold sum2/v xs) end n]]  f [1 2 3]
column3: a local fn as a fold callback, its result bound to another local

column1: def f fn [[xs:List] [Integer] [def keep fn [[p:Any] [Boolean] [p.value gt 2]] size (filter keep/v xs)]]  f [1 2 3 4]
column3: a local fn as a filter predicate (the Function form sees {key value})

column1: def f fn [[xs:List] [List] [def dbl fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 2]] def odd fn [[p:Any] [Boolean] [p.value mod 2 eq 1]] each dbl/v (filter odd/v xs)]]  f [1 2 3 4 5]
column3: TWO body-local fns, one filtering and one mapping — the real pipeline shape

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def g fn [[] [Integer] [7]] def h fn [[] [Integer] [g mul 2]] h]]  f
column3: one body-local fn calls another defined beside it

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def h fn [[] [Integer] [k]] def k 3 end h]]  f
column3: a local fn defined BEFORE the local it reads — a forward ref resolved at call time

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def ev fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [true] [od (n sub 1)]]] def od fn [[n:Integer] [Boolean] [if (n eq 0) [false] [ev (n sub 1)]]] if (ev 4) [1] [0]]]  f
column3: MUTUALLY recursive body-local fns

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a2 fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x add 1] [s:String] [Integer] [size s]] (a2 1) add (a2 'ab')]]  f
column3: a body-local fn with TWO overloads, both dispatched from the same body

column1: # §2  RECURSION with a body-local helper
def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def go fn [[k:Integer a:Integer] [Integer] [if (k lte 0) [a] [go (k sub 1) (a add k)]]] go n 0]]  f 10
column3: the accumulator idiom written as a body-local helper

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def fib fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [if (k lte 1) [k] [(fib (k sub 1)) add (fib (k sub 2))]]] fib n]]  f 10
column3: a body-local fib — tree recursion resolving its own name through the frame

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def n 3 end def go fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [if (k lte 0) [0] [n add (go (k sub 1))]]] go 2]]  f
column3: the recursive local helper CAPTURES a sibling body-local

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def loop2 fn [[k:Integer acc:Integer] [Integer] [if (k eq 0) [acc] [def nxt (acc add k) end loop2 (k sub 1) nxt]]] loop2 n 0]]  f 5
column3: the helper defines its OWN local per frame, then tail-calls itself

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def go fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [if (k lte 0) [0] [k add (go (k sub 1))]]] go n]]  f 4
column3: non-tail recursion in a body-local helper

column1: # §3  a def whose value is COMPUTED
def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def y (x mul 3) end y add 1]]  f 5
column3: a local whose value is computed from a param

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def b (a add 1) end def c (b add a) end c]]  f
column3: a chain of computed locals, each reading the previous

column1: def f fn [[xs:List] [Integer] [def total (0 fold [add] xs) end def n (size xs) end total div n]]  f [1 2 3]
column3: two computed locals combined — the mean idiom

column1: def f fn [[xs:List] [Map] [def n (size xs) end def tot (0 fold [add] xs) end {n: n tot: tot}]]  f [1 2 3]
column3: computed locals assembled into the returned map

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def r (if (n gt 0) [1] [2]) end r add 10]]  f 3
column3: a local whose value is an `if` EXPRESSION (the provenance-safe spelling)

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [String] [def kind (case n [[lt 0] 'neg' 0 'zero' 'pos']) end kind]]  f -3
column3: a local whose value is a `case` expression

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 2 end def r (do [a add 1]) end r]]  f
column3: a local whose value comes from `do` over a code body that reads another local

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def body (codequote [mul 3]) end 0 fold [add] (each body [1 2])]]  f
column3: a local holding an unevaluated code body, spliced into `each`

column1: # §4  REDEFINITION inside a body (and undef)
def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def a 2 end def a 3 end a]]  f
column3: three defs of the same name in one body — the last wins

column1: def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def y 1 end def y (x add y) end y]]  f 5
column3: a redefinition computed from the PREVIOUS binding

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def a (a add 1) end def a (a add 1) end def a (a add 1) end a]]  f
column3: the counter-by-redefinition idiom

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def a 'two' end size a]]  f
column3: a redefinition may change the TYPE of the local

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end undef a end def a 5 end a]]  f
column3: undef then redefine inside one body

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def b 2 end undef a end b]]  f
column3: undef of one local leaves its sibling alone

column1: # §5  a local SHADOWING a param, a module-level name, a module word
def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def x 9 end x]]  f 5
column3: a body-local SHADOWS the param of the same name

column1: def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def y x end def x 9 end y add x]]  f 5
column3: …and the param's value survives in a local bound before the shadow

column1: def scale 10 end def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def scale 3 end x mul scale]]  f 4
column3: a body-local shadows a MODULE-level name

column1: def scale 10 end def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def scale 3 end x mul scale]] end def z (f 4) end scale
column3: …and the module-level binding is intact after the frame exits

column1: def limit 100 end def f fn [[x:Integer] [Boolean] [def limit 3 end x lt limit]]  f 5
column3: the shadow changes the answer the body computes

column1: def cfg {scale:3} end def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def cfg {scale:10} end x mul (cfg.scale)]]  f 2
column3: the shadowed module-level name is a MAP read through a field

column1: def cfg {scale:3} end def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [x mul (cfg.scale)]]  f 2
column3: without a shadow the body reads the module-level map DYNAMICALLY

column1: import module [def dbl fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 2]] export "MM" {dbl: dbl/v}] end def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def dbl fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 3]] dbl x]]  f 4
column3: a body-local fn shadows an imported module's EXPORTED word name

column1: import module [def dbl fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [n mul 2]] export "MM" {dbl: dbl/v}] end def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [MM.dbl x]]  f 4
column3: …the namespaced call is unaffected by any such local

column1: import "boru:string-util" end def f fn [[s:String] [String] [def up fn [[v:String] [String] [StringUtil.upper v]] up s]]  f 'ab'
column3: a body-local fn WRAPPING a namespaced module word

column1: import module [def k 5 end export "MM" {k: k}] end def f fn [[] [Integer] [def MM 9 end MM]]  f
column3: a body-local may NOT shadow an imported module's NAMESPACE

column1: import "boru:math-util" end def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def MathUtil 3 end x mul MathUtil]]  f 5
column3: …the same compile failure for a boru: module namespace

column1: # §6  CONDITIONAL defs inside a branch — the single biggest compiled gap
def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n gt 0) [def r 1 end r add 10] [def r 2 end r add 20]]]  f 3
column3: a branch-local def CONSUMED inside the same branch — provenance stays inside

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [if b [def r 1 end r mul 10] [def r 2 end r mul 100]]]  f false
column3: …the else branch, same shape

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end if (a gt 0) [def b 2 end def c (b mul 3) end c] [0]]]  f
column3: two defs inside one branch, the second computed from the first

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def r (if true [def b 2 end b] [0]) end r add a]]  f
column3: a branch-local def escaping as the `if` EXPRESSION's value

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [if (n gt 0) [def s 'pos' end s size] [def s 'neg' end s size]]]  f 1
column3: a String branch-local measured inside the branch

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [String] [if (n gt 0) [def tag 'big'] [def tag 'small'] end tag]]  f 5
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: a def in EACH branch, read AFTER the if — force-compile: fn f: body result of unknown provenance

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [String] [if (n gt 0) [def tag 'big'] [def tag 'small'] end tag]]  f 0
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …the SAME row on the ELSE path — the pair that a then-arm-always lowering would miscompile

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [String] [def tag 'none' end if (n gt 0) [def tag 'big'] [def tag 'small'] end tag]]  f 5
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …even with the name pre-bound before the branch — same reason

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [String] [def tag 'none' end if (n gt 0) [def tag 'big'] [def tag 'small'] end tag]]  f 0
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …pre-bound, ELSE path — the join must beat the pre-bind, not fall back to it

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def x 1 end if true [def x 9] [] end x]]  f
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: a ONE-sided conditional redefinition — same reason

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def x 1 end if false [def x 9] [] end x]]  f
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …one-sided on the FALSE path — the EMPTY arm must carry the incoming binding through

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end if true [def a 2 end] [] end a]]  f
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …and with an explicit `end` closing the branch body

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end if false [def a 2 end] [] end a]]  f
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …the explicit-`end` spelling on the FALSE path

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [def r 0 end if b [if true [def r 1] [def r 2]] [def r 3] end r]]  f true
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: NESTED conditional defs read after the outer if — same reason

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [def r 0 end if b [if true [def r 1] [def r 2]] [def r 3] end r]]  f false
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …nested, OUTER else taken — the outer join reads an arm the inner if never entered

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [def r 0 end if b [if false [def r 1] [def r 2]] [def r 3] end r]]  f true
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …nested, outer then and INNER else — the inner join feeds the outer one

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def r 0 end if (n gt 0) [def r 1] [def r 2] end r add 10]]  f 3
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: the conditionally-def'd local feeding an operator — force-compile: operand of unknown provenance or not statically materialisable at add

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def r 0 end if (n gt 0) [def r 1] [def r 2] end r add 10]]  f 0
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …the operand spelling on the ELSE path — force-compile: operand of unknown provenance or not statically materialisable at add

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end if true [def a 2] [] end a mul 10]]  f
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …the one-sided spelling of the same operand compile failure, at mul

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end if false [def a 2] [] end a mul 10]]  f
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …one-sided operand, FALSE path — the empty arm's carry-through feeding mul

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def half fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [k div 2]] def q (half n) end if (q gt 1) [def q (half q)] [] end q]]  f 8
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: a local helper plus a conditional REBIND of a local — the combined real-code shape

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def half fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [k div 2]] def q (half n) end if (q gt 1) [def q (half q)] [] end q]]  f 2
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …the local-helper rebind with the condition FALSE — q survives the branch unrebound

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def pick2 fn [[c:Boolean] [Function] [if c [([] => [a])] [([] => [0])]]] def h (pick2 true) end h]]  f
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: a local fn RETURNING a closure from a branch — force-compile: if: then-branch result of unknown provenance

column1: # §6b  CONDITIONALLY BOUND — the name exists only if the arm ran. Every row
#      here MISCOMPILED before 2026-09-21: the check pass runs both arms to
#      type them, so a literal bound in one arm looked unconditional and BAKED,
#      and the compiled program answered the arm's value where the interpreter
#      raises. They are ERROR rows because the program IS wrong on that path;
#      what was wrong was the compiler agreeing with it.
def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [if b [def z 9] [] end z]]  f false
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: the then-arm never ran, so `z` is unbound — answered 9 before the conditional-bind screen

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [if b [] [def z 9] end z]]  f true
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …the ELSE-arm spelling, condition true — also answered 9

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [if b [def z 9] [] end z add 1]]  f false
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …the unbound read feeding an operator — answered 10

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [String] [if b [def z 'hi'] [] end z]]  f false
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …a String local — answered 'hi'; any inert literal bakes, not just numbers

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [if b [def z (1 add 8)] [] end z]]  f false
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: …a COMPUTED bind — leaked a nil as `expected Integer, got <nil>` rather than a value

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [Integer] [if b [def z 9] [] end z]]  f true
column3: DOES NOT COMPILE: the TRUE path of the same program — correct at run time, but the compiler cannot know `b`, so it declines the program rather than bake the arm

column1: def f fn [[b:Boolean] [String] [if b [def tag 'big' tag] [def tag 'small' tag] end]]  f true
column3: …and the read INSIDE the arm still compiles: the binding is live exactly where it was made

column1: # §7  DYNAMIC-SCOPE reads — a callee sees the CALLER frame's bindings
def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 5 end g add 1]] def g fn [[] [Integer] [a mul 2]]  f
column3: a module-level callee reads the CALLER's body-local (dynamic scope, no capture)

column1: def f fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [g]] def g fn [[] [Integer] [x add 1]]  f 41
column3: …and reads the caller's PARAM the same way

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def cfg {n:3} end g]] def g fn [[] [Integer] [cfg.n mul 2]]  f
column3: the dynamically-read caller local is a map, read through a field

column1: def outer3 fn [[] [Integer] [def limit3 4 end mid3]] def mid3 fn [[] [Integer] [inner3]] def inner3 fn [[] [Integer] [limit3 mul 2]]  outer3
column3: the dynamic read reaches TWO frames up, through an intermediate callee

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def g fn [[] [Integer] [def a 2 end h]] def h fn [[] [Integer] [a]]  g]]  f
column3: h is CONSTRUCTED beside a=1 so it captures 1 — the callee's own a=2 does not win

column1: # §8  a local read by a NESTED body — capture, snapshot, transitivity
def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def g fn [[] [Integer] [def b 2 end a add b]] g]]  f
column3: a nested body reads the enclosing body's local (capture) and its own

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def g fn [[] [Integer] [def h fn [[] [Integer] [a]] h]] g]]  f
column3: the capture is TRANSITIVE — two bodies deep

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def g fn [[] [Integer] [def b 2 end def h fn [[] [Integer] [a add b]] h]] g]]  f
column3: the innermost body reads a local from each enclosing frame

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 1 end def g fn [[] [Integer] [def a 2 end def h fn [[] [Integer] [a]] h]] g]]  f
column3: the INNER a shadows the outer for the body nested under it

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def n 5 end def g fn [[] [Integer] [n]] def n 9 end g]]  f
column3: a body-local capture is a SNAPSHOT — the later redefinition does not reach it

column1: def f fn [[] [String] [def kind 'a' end def g fn [[] [String] [kind]] def kind 'b' end g]]  f
column3: …the same snapshot rule over a String local

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def n 1 end def g fn [[] [Integer] [n]] def n 2 end def r (g) end r add n]]  f
column3: snapshot vs current side by side: g sees 1, the body sees 2

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def n 5 end def g ([] => [n]) end def n 9 end g]]  f
column3: a def-bound LAMBDA snapshots the local exactly as the fn form does

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def step 10 end def bump fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [k add step]] def step 100 end bump 5]]  f
column3: a local helper's capture is unaffected by a later rebind of the captured local

column1: def f fn [[n:Integer] [Integer] [def bump fn [[k:Integer] [Integer] [k add step]] def step 10 end bump n]]  f 5
column3: …but a local defined AFTER the helper is a forward ref, resolved dynamically at call time

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 2 end each ([x:Integer] => [x mul a]) [1 2 3] end size]]  f
column3: an each CALLBACK closes over a body-local

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def a 2 end 0 fold ([s:Integer x:Integer] => [s add (x mul a)]) [1 2 3]]]  f
column3: a fold callback closes over a body-local

column1: def f fn [[] [Integer] [def make2 fn [[] [Function] [def secret 42 end ([] => [secret])]] def gg (make2) end gg]]  f
column3: a local factory returns a closure over ITS body-local, called after its frame exits
